metaData.originalTitle: The Pulse: a trend of trying to cut back on AI spend within eng departments?
metaData.title: The Pulse: a trend of trying to cut back on AI spend within eng departments?
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: A growing trend of engineering departments scrutinizing and cutting back on AI spend, as the direct link between AI tool usage and shipped features remains unclear.
metaData.summary: This article from The Pragmatic Engineer newsletter reports on a nascent but significant trend: engineering departments are starting to question and cut back on rapidly growing AI spending, particularly on AI coding tools. It opens with Uber's president questioning the ROI of AI-driven code commits, noting the difficulty in linking metrics like '25% of code commits via AI' to actual shipped features. The article then gathers perspectives from various companies: OpenCode sees surging demand for cheaper model hosting; cutting-edge companies feel forced to pay an 'intelligence premium' but are exploring model routing; DoorDash gives devs responsibility for their token usage; a traditional company imposes monthly limits and downgrades to cheaper models; and startups are buying multiple subscriptions to avoid API costs. The piece concludes by noting a new bottom-up focus on AI efficiency, with engineers experimenting with cheaper models and routing, and predicts that saving on AI costs will become a rewarded metric in performance reviews.

mainPoints.point: The direct ROI of AI coding tools is increasingly being questioned by engineering leaders.
mainPoints.explanation: Uber's president highlights the difficulty in connecting impressive metrics like AI-generated code commits to the delivery of new, useful features for users, making the growing AI spend harder to justify.

mainPoints.point: Companies are adopting diverse strategies to manage AI costs, from model routing to usage limits.
mainPoints.explanation: Strategies range from 'smart' model routing at cutting-edge firms and dev-level token budgets at DoorDash, to hard monthly limits and downgrades to cheaper models at a traditional company, and bulk subscriptions at startups.

mainPoints.point: A bottom-up movement for AI efficiency is emerging among engineers.
mainPoints.explanation: Engineers are increasingly organizing knowledge-sharing sessions on efficient AI use, experimenting with cheaper models and routing, without top-down mandates, suggesting a cultural shift.

mainPoints.point: Saving on AI costs is predicted to become a key performance metric for engineers.
mainPoints.explanation: The article argues that translating AI spend savings into monetary impact will be a clear path for engineers to demonstrate value, similar to how saving on third-party vendor bills was rewarded in the past.

keyQuotes: If you're not able to draw a direct line to [how many] useful features and functionality you're shipping to your users, that tradeoff [on AI spend] becomes harder to justify because AI is not free.
My hunch is that pretty much every company is starting to, or will do soon, ask questions about the massive growth in AI spend; starting with AI coding tools.
There's a touch of irony in how any savings -- for which there might be promotions and pay rises -- will come from the places that actually did the rocketing spending.

relatedArticles.title: The Pulse: ‘Tokenmaxxing’ as a weird new trend
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Tokenmaxxing, the practice of maximizing AI token usage for status and metrics, is a wasteful trend at Meta, Microsoft, and Salesforce, while Shopify offers a more balanced approach with circuit breakers.

relatedArticles.title: The Pulse: Forward deployed engineering heats up again
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: The Pragmatic Engineer analyzes the rising demand for Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) at Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic, arguing the role is shifting from platform engineering to a consultant-like position, creating opportunities for new grads but remaining less attractive to experienced engineers.

relatedArticles.title: Codex for (almost) everything
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI announces a major update to Codex, expanding its capabilities beyond coding to include computer operation, web interaction, image generation, and deeper integration across the software development lifecycle with new features like memory, automations, and over 90 plugins.

relatedArticles.title: The Pulse: Antigravity 2.0 takes ‘IDE’ out of its new IDE
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Google's Antigravity 2.0 launch is a rushed, confusing, and buggy product that removes the IDE interface, copies Codex, and signals Google's continued inability to build credible developer tools.

relatedArticles.title: Introducing Claude Opus 4.7
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Anthropic has released Claude Opus 4.7, a significant upgrade over Opus 4.6 with major improvements in advanced software engineering, vision capabilities, instruction following, and autonomous long-horizon reasoning, while implementing new cyber safeguards and maintaining the same pricing.

relatedArticles.title: The Pulse: AI load breaks GitHub – why not other vendors?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: GitHub's recent severe reliability issues, including a data integrity incident and frequent outages, are attributed to an unexpected surge in load from AI agents, exposing the company's failure to prepare for the AI-driven scale increase that competitors have managed.

relatedArticles.title: Claude Code auto mode: a safer way to skip permissions
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Claude Code's new Auto mode uses a two-stage model-based classifier and prompt-injection probes to autonomously gate dangerous actions, balancing developer productivity with security.

relatedArticles.title: How Claude Code works in large codebases: Best practices and where to start | Claude
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides a comprehensive guide on deploying Claude Code in large codebases, emphasizing that success depends more on the 'harness' of configuration layers (CLAUDE.md, hooks, skills, plugins, LSP, MCP) than on the model alone, and outlines proven patterns for making codebases navigable, maintaining configurations, and assigning organizational ownership.

relatedArticles.title: The Pulse: token spend breaks budgets – what next?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article investigates the rapidly escalating cost of AI tokens across companies of all sizes, revealing a 10x increase in spend over six months and exploring the two dominant strategies companies are adopting: 'let it rip and measure' versus 'curb spending.'

relatedArticles.title: Cursor and SpaceX Partner to Scale AI Coding with Stargate-Class Infrastructure
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Cursor CEO Michael Truell announces a strategic partnership with SpaceX to leverage massive compute infrastructure for scaling the Cursor Composer and building advanced coding models.
